acceptance_criteria: reconnect survives forced disconnect test

tasks.completion_note: Implemented authenticated Capital.com minute OHLC subscriptions for configured epics, bid/ask update normalization, eight-minute WebSocket keepalive, bounded reconnect, and REST backfill beginning at the last observed minute to recover incomplete candles. Forced-disconnect, resubscription, gap-fill, ping, and epic-limit tests pass in GitHub Actions run 37119657855. Ready for Claude review in PR #5. CLAUDE REVIEW 1 (changes requested). Approved as written: epic cap 40, token-bearing messages never logged by this module, 8-minute ping, bounded reconnect backoff, REST backfill from the last observed minute, strict numeric validation, bid and ask both captured, offline tests with forced disconnect. Required changes: (1) Silent-failure risk. Subscribe and ping replies are ignored, so a subscription made with stale session tokens (REST session idle more than 10 minutes) fails without any signal and the socket just sits open. Do all three: (a) call the REST client's ping() before every connection attempt so the tokens are fresh; (b) read the subscribe reply and treat any non-OK status, or any requested epic not confirmed, as a failure that closes the socket and reconnects with a fresh session (log epic names and status only); (c) require a reply to each ping within 30 seconds and treat a missing or non-OK reply as a dead connection. Liveness must rest on ping replies, not on price flow, because markets are legitimately silent when closed. Add tests for stale-token subscribe error, missing ping reply and non-OK ping reply. (2) websockets DEBUG logging prints frames, including the cst and securityToken fields. Force logging.getLogger('websockets') to WARNING at import of this module (and in configure_logging) and add a test that DEBUG records from it cannot be emitted. (3) Exceptions raised inside the on_update callback are currently caught by the generic reconnect handler and look like network errors. Let consumer exceptions propagate out of run_forever (log type only) so a bug in the recorder is visible and supervised, not hidden in a reconnect loop. Add a test. (4) Add scripts/verify_capital_stream.py for the owner to run on the pod: demo-only guard as in verify_capital_demo.py, argument --epic (default US100) and --seconds (default 90), prints redacted JSON only: counts of bid and ask updates, first and last update time, whether ping reply was OK, number of reconnects, and the epic. No tokens, no account data. Document in infra/runpod/README.md that on weekends the owner can pass --epic BTCUSD as a test-only stream (BTCUSD is never added to instruments.yaml and never traded). Live verification on the pod is the acceptance for this task. CODEX REVIEW-CYCLE 1 FIXES: validates REST session before each connection; checks subscribe acknowledgements for OK status and each configured epic; validates immediate and periodic ping acknowledgements with a 30-second timeout; logs websockets at WARNING; logs callback exception type and propagates the original exception; adds the demo-only owner verification script and RunPod instructions. Also addresses automated PR review: naive snapshotTimeUTC is interpreted as UTC and REST gap-fill starts at the earliest side watermark while suppressing per-side duplicates. Full CI run 37120689237 passed (lint, typecheck, migrations, tests, handoff validation, secret scan, Docker/runtime and backup/restore). Code is ready for Claude re-review; live pod verification remains pending under Q-019.

decisions.statement: The LLM never has broker access. Proposals go through the deterministic Risk Guardian, then the Execution Service.

3M candles are produced by resampling 1M because Capital.com has no 3-minute resolution.
HistData is used for hypothesis generation; Capital.com demo forward testing is used for confirmation. HistData is bid-only, M1, EST without DST; convert to UTC on import.
Start with one RunPod pod (ROLE=all, CPU only); split into core and worker, and move to managed Postgres/Redis, before live trading.

Telegram is the primary natural-language channel; the web UI is optional and sits behind the same ChatChannel interface. Decided by Claude on the owner's delegation: Telegram is the interface, with a web chat added later if wanted.
Strategies are declarative specs run in a sandbox; no LLM-written executable code runs in core or execution processes.
Backups: GitHub for code/config/state, HuggingFace for data and results. Never back up secrets.
Account size for risk sizing means account equity (balance plus open P&L).
Starting risk limits: 0.5% risk per trade, 2% max daily loss, 10% max drawdown, 3 concurrent live strategies.

Risk limits and Lab gates can be changed by the owner through natural language, but only via the deterministic SettingsService: allow-listed owner chat, confirmation, hard ceilings baked into the image, tightening immediate, loosening needs a second factor and a cooldown, no loosening while a loss halt is active. LLM agents cannot call or edit it.
GitHub namespace Tarek-Assaf; private repos. Proposed names: ai-trader (GitHub) and ai-trader-data (HuggingFace dataset). HuggingFace username confirmed as Tarek-Assaf.
Reports and alerts go through Telegram plus email (address and method pending, Q-006).

The earlier project is reference material. Fresh repo with the new architecture; audit the old project first (C-005) and adopt pieces selectively. Nothing is adopted without passing this project's tests and safety invariants, and any model or signal from it enters only through the Strategy Lab gates.
v1 timeframes: 1M, 3M and 5M. 3M is resampled from 1M; 15M can be added later through config.
Email reports use SMTP with an app password held as a RunPod Secret (REPORT_EMAIL_TO holds the recipient). Telegram stays the primary channel.
Hard ceilings in config/risk_ceilings.yaml: risk per trade 1.0%, daily loss 4%, drawdown 15%, concurrent live strategies 5.

Reuse of the earlier project follows docs/legacy_audit.md: adapt data QA, tick/spread handling, experiment logging, backtest structure and tests; skip its models, risk manager, paper engine, paper trades and requirements.txt. Models re-enter only through Strategy Lab gates.

Strategy Lab gates use the stricter minimums: Gate 1 at least 300 simulated trades (100 out-of-sample), 5 walk-forward windows, 3 validation periods; Gate 2 at least 4 weeks and 200 demo trades; Gate 3 at least 4 weeks and 100 micro-live trades. Other gate criteria unchanged.

Analyst roster v1 as in ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2: AI analysts (Technical, News and Macro, Critic, Performance) plus code analysts (indicator/pattern engine, execution quality, data quality, Risk Guardian). Instrument knowledge lives in config playbooks.

Phase 0 uses uv 0.6.3 with committed uv.lock and exact direct dependency pins. In ROLE=all, root entrypoint only prepares /workspace ownership, then supervisord, PostgreSQL, Redis and API run as the non-root trader user; PostgreSQL and Redis bind to loopback.

Publish the container image to the private GitHub Container Registry package ghcr.io/tarek-assaf/ai-trader for RunPod. Pull authentication uses a GitHub classic PAT scoped to read:packages; rotate by adding a replacement token to RunPod, confirming image pull and /health, then revoking the old token.

Testing-phase LLM strategy (no live trading): mixed tiers. Cheap tier (small in-pod model or Haiku 4.5) for news sorting, summaries and tagging; mid tier (Haiku 4.5 or Sonnet 5.5) for researcher, analyst and critic; Sonnet 5.5 for the final decision; strongest tier (Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.1) unused until the system is profitable.
